title.zh: 卷一百三十 載記第三十 赫連勃勃
title.raw: 卷一百三十 載記第三十 赫連勃勃 Volume 130 Records 30: Helian Bobo

sentences.zh: 赫連勃勃

translations.literal: Helian Bobo
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo

sentences.zh: 赫連勃勃，字屈孑，匈奴右賢王去卑之後，劉元海之族也。

translations.literal: Helian Bobo, courtesy name Qujie, was a descendant of the Xiongnu Right Worthy King Qubei and a clansman of Liu Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo, styled Qujie, traced his line to the Xiongnu Right Worthy King Qubei and belonged to the same clan as Liu Yuanhai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖武，劉聰世以宗室封樓煩公，拜安北將軍、監鮮卑諸軍事、丁零中郎將，雄據肆盧川。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wu, during the reign of Liu Cong, was enfeoffed as Duke of Loufan for his status within the imperial clan, appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Supervisor of Xianbei Military Affairs, and Central Commandant of the Dingling, and dominated the Silu River region.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wu, in Liu Cong's day, received the title Duke of Loufan as a member of the imperial house and held the posts of General Who Pacifies the North, overseer of Xianbei military affairs, and Central Commandant of the Dingling, ruling the Silu River country as a regional power.

sentences.zh: 為代王猗盧所敗，遂出塞表。

translations.literal: He was defeated by the Dai king Tuoba Yilu and fled beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated by Dai King Tuoba Yilu, he withdrew beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 祖豹子招集種落，復為諸部之雄，石季龍遣使就拜平北將軍、左賢王、丁零單于。

translations.literal: His grandfather Baozi gathered the tribal peoples and again became chief among the tribes; Shi Jilong sent envoys to appoint him on the spot as General Who Pacifies the North, Left Worthy King, and Chanyu of the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Baozi rallied the tribes and once more rose to leadership among them; Shi Jilong dispatched envoys to invest him as General Who Pacifies the North, Left Worthy King, and Chanyu of the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 父衛辰入居塞內，苻堅以為西單于，督攝河西諸虜，屯於代來城。

translations.literal: His father Wei Chen entered and settled within the frontier; Fu Jian made him Western Chanyu, put him in charge of the various barbarians west of the river, and garrisoned him at Dailai city.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei Chen moved inside the frontier, where Fu Jian named him Western Chanyu, entrusted him with the barbarian peoples of Hexi, and stationed him at Dailai.

sentences.zh: 及堅國亂，遂有朔方之地，控弦之士三萬八千。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian's state fell into turmoil, he secured the Shuofang region and had thirty-eight thousand bow-bearing warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fu Jian's realm collapsed into disorder, he held Shuofang with thirty-eight thousand archers under arms.

sentences.zh: 後魏師伐之，辰令其子力俟提距戰，為魏所敗。

translations.literal: Later Wei forces attacked him; Chen ordered his son Lishiti to resist in battle, and they were defeated by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei marched against him, Chen sent his son Lishiti to hold the line, but Wei broke them.

sentences.zh: 魏人乘勝濟河，克代來，執辰殺之。

translations.literal: The Wei troops crossed the river in pursuit of victory, captured Dailai, seized Chen, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei crossed the river on the momentum of victory, took Dailai, captured Chen, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 勃勃乃奔于叱幹部。

translations.literal: Bobo thereupon fled to the Chigan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo fled to the Chigan tribe.

sentences.zh: 叱幹他鬥伏送勃勃于魏。

translations.literal: The Chigan chief Tadoufu sent Bobo to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tadoufu of the Chigan delivered Bobo to Wei.

sentences.zh: 他鬥伏兄子阿利先戍大洛川。

translations.literal: Tadoufu's nephew Ali had already been garrisoned at the Daluo River.
translations.idiomatic: Tadoufu's nephew Ali was already stationed on the Daluo River.

sentences.zh: 聞將送勃勃，馳諫曰：「鳥雀投人，尚宜濟免，況勃勃國破家亡，歸命於我？

translations.literal: Hearing that Bobo was to be handed over, he raced to remonstrate, saying, "When birds come seeking refuge among people, one ought still to aid and spare them—how much more so when Bobo, his state shattered and his family destroyed, has entrusted himself to us?
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Bobo was to be turned over, he rode in haste to protest: "Even a sparrow that flies to a man deserves mercy—how much more a man whose kingdom is gone and whose house is ruined, who has come to us for shelter?

sentences.zh: 縱不能容，猶宜任其所奔。

translations.literal: Even if we cannot harbor him, we should at least let him flee whither he will.
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot keep him, we should at least let him go where he chooses.

sentences.zh: 今執而送之，深非仁者之舉。

translations.literal: To seize and deliver him now would be deeply contrary to the conduct of the humane.
translations.idiomatic: To bind him and send him off would be a deed far from humane.

sentences.zh: 」他鬥伏懼為魏所責，弗從。

translations.literal: Tadoufu, fearing blame from Wei, did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tadoufu, afraid Wei would hold him accountable, refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 阿利潛遣勁勇篡勃勃于路，送于姚興高平公沒奕于，奕于以女妻之。

translations.literal: Ali secretly sent fierce warriors to abduct Bobo on the road and deliver him to Yao Xing's Duke of Gaoping, Moyiyu; Moyiyu gave his daughter to Bobo in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ali secretly sent bold men to snatch Bobo on the road and convey him to Moyiyu, Duke of Gaoping under Yao Xing, who gave Bobo his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 勃勃身長八尺五寸，腰帶十圍，性辯慧，美風儀。

translations.literal: Bobo stood eight chi and five cun in height, his waist girdle ten wei in circumference; by nature he was eloquent and clever, with handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo stood eight feet five inches tall, with a waist ten handspans around; he was quick-witted and eloquent, and carried himself with striking grace.

sentences.zh: 興見而奇之，深加禮敬，拜驍騎將軍，加奉車都尉，常參軍國大議，寵遇逾於勳舊。

translations.literal: Xing saw him and found him extraordinary, treating him with deep courtesy; he appointed him General of Valiant Cavalry and added Chariot Commandant; he regularly participated in great state councils, and the favor shown him exceeded that given to meritorious veterans.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was struck by him at once, honored him lavishly, and made him General of Valiant Cavalry with the additional title Chariot Commandant; Bobo took part in every major council of war and state, and was favored beyond the old servants of merit.

sentences.zh: 興弟邕言于興曰：「勃勃天性不仁，難以親近。

translations.literal: Xing's younger brother Yong said to Xing, "Bobo's nature is cruel and lacks humanity—he is difficult to draw near.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's younger brother Yong said to him, "Bobo is ruthless by nature and not a man one can trust.

sentences.zh: 陛下寵遇太甚，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty favors him excessively—I find it puzzling.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty honors him far too much; I cannot make sense of it.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「勃勃有濟世之才，吾方收其藝用，與之共平天下，有何不可！

translations.literal: Xing said, "Bobo has talent to bring order to the age—I am just now harnessing his abilities to pacify the realm together with him—what is wrong with that!
translations.idiomatic: Xing replied, "Bobo has the talent to set the age aright. I mean to use what he can do and win the realm with him—what harm is there in that?

sentences.zh: 」乃以勃勃為安遠將軍，封陽川侯，使助沒奕于鎮高平，以三城、朔方雜夷及衛辰部眾三萬配之，使為伐魏偵候。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Bobo General Who Pacifies the Distant, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yangchuan, had him assist Moyiyu in garrisoning Gaoping, assigned him thirty thousand troops including the mixed barbarians of Sancheng and Shuofang and Wei Chen's followers, and had him serve as a scout for attacking Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Bobo General Who Pacifies the Distant and Marquis of Yangchuan, set him to aid Moyiyu in holding Gaoping, and gave him thirty thousand men drawn from the mixed tribes of Sancheng and Shuofang and from Wei Chen's following, with orders to reconnoiter against Wei.

sentences.zh: 姚邕固諫以為不可。

translations.literal: Yao Yong firmly remonstrated that this was inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yong pressed his objections and said it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 興曰：「卿何以知其性氣？

translations.literal: Xing said, "How do you know his temperament?
translations.idiomatic: Xing asked, "How do you know what sort of man he is?

sentences.zh: 」邕曰：「勃勃奉上慢，禦眾殘，貪暴無親，輕為去就，寵之逾分，終為邊害。

translations.literal: Yong said, "Bobo is disrespectful toward his superiors, cruel toward his followers, greedy and violent without loyalty, and fickle in his alliances—favor him beyond his due and he will ultimately become a frontier calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Yong answered, "He is slack toward his lord, harsh with his men, greedy, brutal, and faithless, and he shifts allegiance lightly. Honor him beyond measure and he will become a scourge on the borderlands."

sentences.zh: 」興乃止。

translations.literal: Xing then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xing held back and did not proceed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以勃勃為持節、安北將軍、五原公，配以三交五部鮮卑及雜虜二萬餘落，鎮朔方。

translations.literal: Before long, he appointed Bobo Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Duke of Wuyuan, assigned him more than twenty thousand tribes of the three-jiao Wubu Xianbei and various barbarians, and stationed him in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he made Bobo Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Duke of Wuyuan, gave him more than twenty thousand households of the three-jiao Wubu Xianbei and other barbarian peoples, and posted him in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 時河西鮮卑杜崘獻馬八千匹于姚興，濟河，至大城，勃勃留之，召其眾三萬餘人偽獵高平川，襲殺沒奕於而並其眾，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: At that time the Hexi Xianbei Du Lun presented eight thousand horses to Yao Xing, crossed the river, and reached Dacheng; Bobo detained him, summoned his more than thirty thousand followers under pretense of hunting on the Gaoping River, attacked and killed Moyiyu and absorbed his forces, and his army reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Hexi Xianbei chief Du Lun brought eight thousand horses as tribute to Yao Xing, crossed the river, and came to Dacheng. Bobo held him there, called up his own force of more than thirty thousand under the guise of a hunt on the Gaoping River, struck and killed Moyiyu, took over his troops, and raised his following to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，僭稱天王、大單于，赦其境內，建元曰龍昇，署置百官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi, he presumptuously styled himself Heavenly King and Grand Chanyu, amnestied his territory, established the era name Longsheng, and installed officials throughout the government.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yixi he declared himself Heavenly King and Grand Chanyu, proclaimed a general amnesty, took the era name Longsheng, and appointed a full roster of officials.

sentences.zh: 自以匈奴夏後氏之苗裔也，國稱大夏。

translations.literal: Considering himself a descendant of the Xiongnu and the Xia dynasty, he named his state Great Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from the Xiongnu and from the house of Xia, and named his state Great Xia.

sentences.zh: 以其長兄右地代為丞相、代公，次兄力俟提為大將軍、魏公，叱幹阿利為御史大夫、梁公，弟阿利羅引為征南將軍、司隸校尉，若門為尚書令，叱以鞬為征西將軍、尚書左僕射，乙鬥為征北將軍、尚書右僕射，自余以次授任。

translations.literal: He made his eldest brother Youdidai chancellor and Duke of Dai, his second brother Lishiti grand general and Duke of Wei, Chigan Ali censor-in-chief and Duke of Liang, his younger brother Aliluoyin General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Masters of Writing, Ruomen Director of the Masters of Writing, Chiyijian General Who Conquers the West and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Yidou General Who Conquers the North and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and assigned the rest in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his eldest brother Youdidai chancellor and Duke of Dai, his second brother Lishiti grand general and Duke of Wei, Chigan Ali censor-in-chief and Duke of Liang, his younger brother Aliluoyin General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Masters of Writing, Ruomen Director of the Masters of Writing, Chiyijian General Who Conquers the West and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Yidou General Who Conquers the North and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and filled the remaining posts in rank below them.

sentences.zh: 其年，討鮮卑薛幹等三部，破之，降眾萬數千。

translations.literal: That year he attacked the three Xianbei tribes including Xuegan, defeated them, and received the submission of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he campaigned against the three Xianbei tribes led by Xuegan, broke them, and accepted the surrender of many thousands.

sentences.zh: 進討姚興三城已北諸戍，斬其將楊丕、姚石生等。

translations.literal: Advancing, he attacked the garrisons north of Sancheng under Yao Xing and beheaded the generals Yang Pi and Yao Shisheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward against Yao Xing's posts north of Sancheng, killing the generals Yang Pi, Yao Shisheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 諸將諫固險，不從，又復言於勃勃曰：「陛下將欲經營宇內，南取長安，宜先固根本，使人心有所憑系，然後大業可成。

translations.literal: The generals remonstrated, urging him to hold secure positions, but he would not listen; they again said to Bobo, "If Your Majesty intends to manage affairs within the realm and march south to take Chang'an, you should first secure the root foundation so that the people have something to rely upon—only then can the great enterprise succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged him to dig in and hold defensible ground, but he refused. They spoke to him again: "If Your Majesty means to rule the realm and seize Chang'an in the south, you must first make the foundation firm so that hearts have something to cling to. Only then can the great work stand.

sentences.zh: 高平險固，山川沃饒，可以都也。

translations.literal: Gaoping is perilous and secure, its mountains and rivers rich and fertile—it can serve as a capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping is strong by nature, its land fertile—fit to be your capital.

sentences.zh: 」勃勃曰：「卿徒知其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: Bobo said, "You know only one part and not the other.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo said, "You see one thing and miss the other.

sentences.zh: 吾大業草創，眾旅未多，姚興亦一時之雄，關中未可圖也。

translations.literal: My great enterprise is newly founded and my forces are still few; Yao Xing too is a hero of the age—the Guanzhong region cannot yet be taken.
translations.idiomatic: My state is still in its first days and my army is small. Yao Xing is a formidable man of his time, and Guanzhong is not yet within reach.

sentences.zh: 且其諸鎮用命，我若專固一城，彼必並力於我，眾非其敵，亡可立待。

translations.literal: Moreover his garrisons obey his orders; if I concentrate on holding a single city, he is sure to bring all his strength against me—I cannot match his numbers, and destruction would come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, his frontier posts answer his call. If I lock myself into one fortress, he will throw every force at me. I cannot match him in numbers, and ruin would follow quickly.

sentences.zh: 吾以雲騎風馳，出其不意，救前則擊其後，救後則擊其前，使彼疲於奔命，我則游食自若，不及十年，嶺北、河東盡我有也。

translations.literal: I shall ride like clouds and gallop like wind, strike where they do not expect; if they rescue the front I shall hit the rear, if they rescue the rear I shall hit the front, wear them out with constant running to and fro while I live off the land at ease—in less than ten years all the country north of the mountains and east of the river will be mine.
translations.idiomatic: I will move like wind-driven cavalry and strike where no one looks for me. Let them rush to save the van and I will fall on the rear; let them save the rear and I will fall on the van. I will keep them exhausted while my men forage freely. In less than ten years everything north of the ridges and east of the river will be mine.

sentences.zh: 待姚興死後，徐取長安。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing is dead, I shall take Chang'an at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Xing dies, I will take Chang'an in my own time.

sentences.zh: 姚泓凡弱小兒，擒之方略，已在吾計中矣。

translations.literal: Yao Hong is a weak and childish man—the plan to capture him is already settled in my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong is a feeble boy. The way to seize him is already laid in my mind.

sentences.zh: 昔軒轅氏亦遷居無常二十餘年，豈獨我乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor too moved his dwelling without fixed abode for more than twenty years—am I alone in this!
translations.idiomatic: Even the Yellow Emperor wandered without a fixed seat for more than twenty years—why should I alone be blamed for it!

sentences.zh: 」於是侵掠嶺北，嶺北諸城門不晝啟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raided north of the mountains, and north of the mountains the city gates were not opened in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: He then harried the country north of the ridges, and there the city gates stayed shut even by day.

sentences.zh: 興歎曰：「吾不用黃兒之言，以至於此！

translations.literal: Xing sighed and said, "Had I heeded Yellow Boy's words, I would not have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sighed, "Had I listened to Yellow Boy, I would never have come to this pass!

sentences.zh: 」黃兒，姚邕小字也。

translations.literal: "Yellow Boy" was Yao Yong's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "Yellow Boy" was the childhood name of Yao Yong.

sentences.zh: 勃勃初僭號，求婚於禿髮傉檀，傉檀弗許。

translations.literal: When Bobo first assumed his royal title, he sought marriage with Tufa Rutan, but Rutan refused.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Bobo first took royal rank, he asked Tufa Rutan for a marriage alliance, and Rutan declined.

sentences.zh: 勃勃怒，率騎二萬伐之，自楊非至於支陽三百餘里，殺傷萬餘人，驅掠二萬七千口、牛馬羊數十萬而還。

translations.literal: Bobo in anger led twenty thousand horsemen to attack him, from Yangfei to Zhiyang a distance of more than three hundred li, killing and wounding more than ten thousand men and driving off twenty-seven thousand captives and several hundred thousand cattle, sheep, and horses before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Bobo led twenty thousand cavalry against him. From Yangfei to Zhiyang—more than three hundred li—he killed and wounded over ten thousand men, carried off twenty-seven thousand people, and drove away tens of thousands of cattle, sheep, and horses before turning back.

sentences.zh: 傉檀率眾追之，其將焦朗謂傉檀曰：「勃勃天姿雄驁，禦軍齊肅，未可輕也。

translations.literal: Rutan led his army in pursuit; his general Jiao Lang said to Rutan, "Bobo is by nature bold and fierce, and his command of troops is strict and orderly—he must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan pursued with his host. His officer Jiao Lang warned him, "Bobo is a born warrior, and his army is disciplined and hard to break. Do not underestimate him.

sentences.zh: 今因抄掠之資，率思歸之士，人自為戰，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: Now, with the spoils of plunder behind them and men eager to return home, each will fight for himself—it will be hard to contend with them in open battle.
translations.idiomatic: They are laden with booty and filled with men who want to go home. Each soldier will fight for himself. It will be hard to meet them head on.

sentences.zh: 不如從溫圍北渡，趣萬斛堆，阻水結營，制其咽喉，百戰百勝之術也。

translations.literal: It would be better to cross north from Wenwei, make for Wanhudui, and encamp where the water blocks their path, controlling their throat—this is the tactic that wins a hundred battles out of a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Better to cross north from Wenwei, strike for Wanhudui, and camp where the river narrows their road. Hold the choke point—that is the way to win every fight.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀將賀連怒曰：「勃勃以死亡之餘，率烏合之眾，犯順結禍，幸有大功。

translations.literal: Rutan's general Helian Nu said, "Bobo is leading the remnant of the defeated, a mob hastily gathered together; he has offended the right order and brought disaster on himself, and only by luck has he won a great success.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan's officer Helian Nu said, "Bobo commands the wreckage of defeat, a crowd patched together overnight. He has defied heaven and courted ruin, and only by fortune gained a great victory.

sentences.zh: 今牛羊塞路，財寶若山，窘弊之餘，人懷貪競，不能督厲士眾以抗我也。

translations.literal: Now cattle and sheep choke the roads and treasure piles like mountains; worn and exhausted as they are, the men are greedy and contentious—they cannot be driven to stand firm against us.
translations.idiomatic: Now their road is blocked with livestock and their wagons heaped with plunder. Exhausted as they are, the men are greedy and unruly. He cannot keep them in line to face us.

sentences.zh: 我以大軍臨之，必土崩魚潰。

translations.literal: When I bring the main army down on them, they are sure to collapse like a wall of earth or fish in a drained pond.
translations.idiomatic: When my main force falls on them, they will break like a crumbling dike or fish stranded in a dry pool.

sentences.zh: 今引軍避之，示敵以弱。

translations.literal: To withdraw the army now and avoid them would show the enemy weakness.
translations.idiomatic: To pull back now would show them we are afraid.

sentences.zh: 我眾氣銳，宜在速追。

translations.literal: Our men's spirit is sharp—we should pursue swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are eager. We should chase them at once.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「吾追計決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: Rutan said, "My mind is made up to pursue—I behead anyone who dares remonstrate!
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "My decision stands. Anyone who argues against the pursuit dies!

sentences.zh: 」勃勃聞而大喜，乃于陽武下陝鑿淩埋車以塞路。

translations.literal: Bobo, hearing this, was greatly pleased; he then at Yangwu dug trenches, buried wagons, and blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Bobo heard this he was delighted. At Yangwu he dug ditches, buried carts, and blocked the way.

sentences.zh: 傉檀遣善射者射之，中勃勃左臂。

translations.literal: Rutan sent skilled archers to shoot at him, and one struck Bobo in the left arm.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sent his best bowmen against him, and one arrow hit Bobo in the left arm.

sentences.zh: 勃勃乃勒眾逆擊，大敗之，追奔八十餘里，殺傷萬計，斬其大將十餘人，以為京觀，號「髑髏台」，還於嶺北。

translations.literal: Bobo then rallied his troops and counterattacked, inflicting a great defeat; he pursued the fleeing enemy for more than eighty li, killing and wounding beyond count, beheaded more than ten of their great generals, built a mound of skulls called the "Skull Platform," and returned north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo wheeled his men and counterattacked, crushing them. He chased the rout more than eighty li, killing and wounding beyond number, took the heads of more than ten senior commanders, and raised a mound of skulls he named the Skull Platform before withdrawing north of the ridges.

sentences.zh: 勃勃與姚興將張佛生戰于青石原，又敗之，俘斬五千七百人。

translations.literal: Bobo fought Yao Xing's general Zhang Fusheng at Qing Shi Plain and again defeated him, capturing and killing five thousand seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: At Qing Shi Plain Bobo fought Yao Xing's general Zhang Fusheng, defeated him again, and killed or captured five thousand seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 興遣將齊難率眾二萬來伐，勃勃退如河曲。

translations.literal: Xing dispatched the general Qi Nan at the head of twenty thousand men to attack; Bobo withdrew toward the river bend.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent General Qi Nan with twenty thousand men against him, and Bobo fell back toward the river bend.

sentences.zh: 難以去勃勃既遠，縱兵掠野，勃勃潛軍覆之，俘獲七千餘人，收其戎馬兵杖。

translations.literal: Qi Nan, thinking Bobo was already far away, let his troops plunder the countryside; Bobo secretly moved his army to envelop them, capturing more than seven thousand men and seizing their horses, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Bobo was already distant, Qi Nan allowed his men to ravage the fields. Bobo slipped a force behind him, took more than seven thousand prisoners, and seized horses, armor, and arms.

sentences.zh: 難引軍而退，勃勃復追擊於木城，拔之，擒難，俘其將士萬有三千，戎馬萬匹。

translations.literal: Qi Nan led his army in retreat; Bobo again pursued and attacked him at Mucheng, captured the city, seized Qi Nan, and took thirteen thousand of his officers and soldiers and ten thousand horses captive.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan withdrew, but Bobo pursued him to Mucheng, stormed the place, captured Qi Nan, and took thirteen thousand soldiers and ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 嶺北夷夏降附者數萬計，勃勃於是拜置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Han peoples north of the mountains submitted to him by the tens of thousands; Bobo thereupon appointed and installed local administrators to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of tribesmen and settlers north of the ridges came over to him, and Bobo appointed magistrates to govern them.

sentences.zh: 勃勃又率騎二萬入高岡，及于五井，掠平涼雜胡七千餘戶以配後軍，進屯依力川。

translations.literal: Bobo again led twenty thousand horsemen into Gaogang and as far as Wujing, plundering more than seven thousand households of mixed barbarians in Pingliang to assign to the rear guard, and advanced to encamp at Yili River.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo led twenty thousand cavalry into Gaogang and on to Wujing, carried off more than seven thousand mixed barbarian households from Pingliang for his rear guard, and moved forward to camp on the Yili River.

sentences.zh: 姚興來伐，至三城，勃勃候興諸軍未集，率騎擊之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing came to attack and reached Sancheng; Bobo waited until Xing's various armies had not yet assembled and led his cavalry to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched against him and reached Sancheng. Bobo watched until Xing's columns were still scattered, then led his cavalry in a sudden blow.

sentences.zh: 興大懼，遣其將姚文宗距戰，勃勃偽退，設伏以待之。

translations.literal: Xing was greatly afraid and sent his general Yao Wenzong to resist; Bobo feigned retreat and set an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was terrified and sent General Yao Wenzong to hold him off. Bobo pretended to flee and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 興遣其將姚榆生等追之，伏兵夾擊，皆擒之。

translations.literal: Xing sent his generals Yao Yusheng and others in pursuit; the hidden troops attacked from both sides and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xing sent Yao Yusheng and others in pursuit, but troops hidden on both flanks sprang up and took them all.

sentences.zh: 興將王奚聚羌胡三千餘戶於敕奇堡，勃勃進攻之。

translations.literal: Xing's general Wang Xi had gathered more than three thousand households of Qiang and barbarians at Chiqi Fortress; Bobo advanced to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's officer Wang Xi had gathered more than three thousand Qiang and barbarian households at Chiqi Fortress, and Bobo marched to besiege it.

sentences.zh: 奚驍悍有膂力，短兵接戰，勃勃之眾多為所傷。

translations.literal: Xi was fierce and strong, fighting at close quarters; many of Bobo's men were wounded by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi was a brutal fighter in close combat, and many of Bobo's soldiers fell to him.

sentences.zh: 於是堰斷其水，堡人窘迫，執奚出降。

translations.literal: Thereupon they dammed and cut off the water supply; the people in the fortress were hard pressed, seized Xi, and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo's men then dammed the stream that fed the fort. Trapped without water, the defenders seized Wang Xi and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 勃勃謂奚曰：「卿忠臣也！

translations.literal: Bobo said to Xi, "You are a loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: Bobo told Wang Xi, "You are a faithful servant!

sentences.zh: 朕方與卿共平天下。

translations.literal: I am just about to win the realm together with you.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to settle the realm with men like you.

sentences.zh: 」奚曰：「若蒙大恩，速死為惠。

translations.literal: Xi said, "If I receive great grace, a quick death would be the greater kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi answered, "If Your Majesty would show mercy, let it be a swift death.

sentences.zh: 」乃與所親數十人自刎而死。

translations.literal: He then, together with several dozen of his close followers, cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he and several dozen of his companions drew their blades and killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 勃勃又攻興將金洛生於黃石固，彌姐豪地于我羅城，皆拔之，徙七千餘家於大城，以其丞相右地代領幽州牧以鎮之。

translations.literal: Bobo again attacked Yao Xing's general Jin Luosheng at Huangshi Fort and Mijie Haodi at Wuluocheng, captured both, moved more than seven thousand households to Dacheng, and had his chancellor Youdidai serve as Governor of Youzhou to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo attacked Yao Xing's general Jin Luosheng at Huangshi Fort and Mijie Haodi at Wuluocheng, took both places, relocated more than seven thousand households to Dacheng, and put his chancellor Youdidai in charge as Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣其尚書金纂率騎一萬攻平涼，姚興來救，纂為興所敗，死之。

translations.literal: He dispatched his Director of the Masters of Writing Jin Zuan at the head of ten thousand horsemen to attack Pingliang; Yao Xing came to the rescue, defeated Zuan, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Director of the Masters of Writing Jin Zuan with ten thousand cavalry against Pingliang. Yao Xing marched to relieve the city, broke Jin Zuan, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 勃勃兄子左將軍羅提率步騎一萬攻興將姚廣都于定陽，克之，坑將士四千餘人，以女弱為軍賞。

translations.literal: Bobo's nephew, Left General Luoti, led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yao Xing's general Yao Guangdu at Dingyang, captured it, buried alive more than four thousand officers and soldiers, and distributed the women and children as rewards to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo's nephew Luoti, Left General, led ten thousand foot and horse against Yao Guangdu at Dingyang, took the city, entombed more than four thousand soldiers alive, and gave the women and children to his troops as booty.

sentences.zh: 拜廣都為太常。

translations.literal: He appointed Guangdu Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He made Guangdu Director of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 勃勃又攻興將姚壽都于清水城，壽都奔上邽，徙其人萬六千家於大城。

translations.literal: Bobo again attacked Yao Xing's general Yao Shoudu at Qingshui city; Shoudu fled to Shanggui, and Bobo moved sixteen thousand six hundred of the inhabitants to Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo attacked Yao Shoudu at Qingshui. Shoudu fled to Shanggui, and Bobo resettled sixteen thousand six hundred of the local people in Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊難、姚廣都謀叛，皆誅之。

translations.literal: That year Qi Nan and Yao Guangdu plotted rebellion; both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qi Nan and Yao Guangdu plotted revolt, and both were put to death.

sentences.zh: 姚興將姚詳棄三城，南奔大蘇。

translations.literal: Yao Xing's general Yao Xiang abandoned Sancheng and fled south to Dasu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's general Yao Xiang abandoned Sancheng and fled south to Dasu.

sentences.zh: 勃勃遣其將平東鹿奕於要擊之，執詳，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Bobo sent his general Pingdong Luyiyu to intercept him on the road, captured Xiang, and took all his followers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo sent General Pingdong Luyiyu to cut him off, seized Yao Xiang, and captured his entire force.

sentences.zh: 詳至，勃勃數而斬之。

translations.literal: When Xiang arrived, Bobo rebuked him and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xiang was brought in, Bobo denounced him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 其年，勃勃率騎三萬攻安定，與姚興將楊佛嵩戰于青石北原，敗之，降其眾四萬五千，獲戎馬二萬匹。

translations.literal: That year Bobo led thirty thousand horsemen to attack Anding and fought Yao Xing's general Yang Fusong on the north plain of Qing Shi, defeated him, received the submission of forty-five thousand of his followers, and captured twenty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: That year Bobo led thirty thousand cavalry against Anding and on the north plain of Qing Shi defeated Yao Xing's general Yang Fusong, accepted the surrender of forty-five thousand of his men, and took twenty thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 進攻姚興將党智隆於東鄉，降之，署智隆光祿勳，徙其三千餘戶於貳城。

translations.literal: Advancing, he attacked Yao Xing's general Dang Zhilong at Dongxiang, received his surrender, appointed Zhilong Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and moved more than three thousand of his households to Ercheng.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on against Dang Zhilong at Dongxiang, accepted his surrender, made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and resettled more than three thousand of his households at Ercheng.

sentences.zh: 姚興鎮北參軍王買德來奔。

translations.literal: Wang Maide, Adjutant to Yao Xing's northern garrison commander, came over to Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maide, staff officer to Yao Xing's northern frontier command, defected to Bobo.

sentences.zh: 勃勃謂買德曰：「朕大禹之後，世居幽、朔。

translations.literal: Bobo said to Maide, "I am a descendant of Yu the Great; for generations my house has dwelt in You and Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo told Wang Maide, "I am descended from Yu the Great. My forebears have long held the northern lands.

sentences.zh: 祖宗重暉，常與漢、魏為敵國。

translations.literal: Our ancestors, heavy with glory, were constantly rival states to Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In their days of power they stood as equals to Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 中世不競，受制於人。

translations.literal: In the middle generations they could not contend and fell under the control of others.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations could not keep pace and were forced to serve others.

sentences.zh: 逮朕不肖，不能紹隆先構，國破家亡，流離漂虜。

translations.literal: Now that I am unworthy and cannot continue and enlarge what my ancestors built, my state is destroyed and my family lost, and I have wandered as a captive in exile.
translations.idiomatic: I have lacked the strength to restore what my fathers built. My kingdom was broken, my house was ruined, and I was driven into exile as a captive.

sentences.zh: 今將應運而興，復大禹之業，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Now I am about to rise with the times and restore the enterprise of Yu the Great—what do you think of this?
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to rise with fortune and renew the work of Yu the Great. What do you say to that?

sentences.zh: 」買德曰：「自皇晉失統，神器南移，群雄嶽峙，人懷問鼎，況陛下奕葉載德，重光朔野，神武超於漢皇，聖略邁于魏祖，而不於天啟之機建成大業乎！

translations.literal: Maide said, "Since the Jin lost the mandate and the sacred vessel moved south, heroes have stood like mountain peaks and every man has harbored the thought of seizing the throne—how much more so when Your Majesty, generation after generation bearing virtue, has restored glory in the northern wilds, with divine martial prowess surpassing the Han emperors and sage strategy exceeding the Wei founders—yet would you not, at heaven's opening moment, complete the great enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maide answered, "Since Jin lost the mandate and the imperial regalia went south, strong men have risen on every side and every heart has turned toward the throne. Your Majesty carries merit through many generations and has brought light again to the northern frontier. Your warlike genius outshines the Han emperors and your design surpasses the founders of Wei. How can heaven's moment pass without your completing the great work?

sentences.zh: 今秦政雖衰，籓鎮猶固，深願蓄力待時，詳而後舉。

translations.literal: Though Qin's government is now in decline, its frontier garrisons are still firm—I deeply wish that you would gather strength and wait for the right time, plan carefully, and then act.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's power may be fading, but its border commands still hold. I beg Your Majesty to store up strength, watch the hour, and move only after careful planning.

sentences.zh: 」勃勃善之，拜軍師中郎將。

translations.literal: Bobo approved of this and appointed him Military Adviser Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo was pleased and made him Military Adviser Commandant.

sentences.zh: 乃赦其境內，改元為鳳翔，以叱幹阿利領將作大匠，發嶺北夷夏十萬人，于朔方水北、黑水之南營起都城。

translations.literal: He thereupon amnestied his territory, changed the era name to Fengxiang, put Chigan Ali in charge as Director of Palace Construction, and mobilized one hundred thousand barbarian and Han people north of the mountains to build a capital on the north bank of the Shuofang River and south of the Black Water.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed another amnesty, changed the era name to Fengxiang, appointed Chigan Ali Director of Palace Construction, and drafted one hundred thousand tribesmen and settlers north of the ridges to raise a capital on the north bank of the Shuofang River and south of the Black Water.

sentences.zh: 勃勃自言：「朕方統一天下，君臨萬邦，可以統萬為名。

translations.literal: Bobo himself said, "I am just now about to unify the realm and rule the myriad states—it can be named Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo declared, "I mean to unite the realm and rule every land under heaven. Let the city be called Tongwan—Unified Ten Thousand.

sentences.zh: 」阿利性尤工巧，然殘忍刻暴，乃蒸土築城，錐入一寸，即殺作者而並築之。

translations.literal: Ali was especially skilled in craftsmanship, yet cruel, harsh, and violent; he steamed earth to build the walls, and if a probe sank one cun into the wall, he killed the builder and had the body built into the wall together with the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Ali was a master craftsman but savage by nature. He steamed earth to raise the walls, and whenever an awl sank one inch into the masonry he killed the builder and built the corpse into the wall along with the earth.

sentences.zh: 勃勃以為忠，故委以營繕之任。

translations.literal: Bobo considered this loyalty and therefore entrusted him with the task of construction.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo took this for loyalty and therefore put him in charge of building the city.

sentences.zh: 又造五兵之器，精銳尤甚。

translations.literal: He also made weapons of the five kinds, their keen edge especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged weapons of every kind, their edges surpassingly sharp.

sentences.zh: 既成呈之，工匠必有死者：射甲不入，即斬弓人；

translations.literal: When they were finished and presented, craftsmen were sure to die: if an arrow did not pierce armor, the bow-maker was beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: When weapons were finished and tested, craftsmen died: if an arrow failed to pierce armor, the bow-maker was beheaded;

sentences.zh: 如其入也，便斬鎧匠。

translations.literal: if it did pierce, the armorer was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: if it pierced, the armorer was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又造百練剛刀，為龍雀大環，號曰「大夏龍雀」，銘其背曰：「古之利器，吳、楚湛盧。

translations.literal: He also made hundred-fold tempered steel blades, with dragon-sparrow great rings, styled "Great Xia Dragon Sparrow"; on the back was inscribed: "Weapons of old—Wu and Chu had Zhanlu."
translations.idiomatic: He forged hundred-fold steel blades called Great Xia Dragon Sparrow, inscribed on the back: "Ancient Wu and Chu prized Zhanlu."

sentences.zh: 大夏龍雀，名冠神都。

translations.literal: Great Xia Dragon Sparrow, its name crowns the divine capital.
translations.idiomatic: Great Xia Dragon Sparrow—its name crowns the divine capital.

sentences.zh: 可以懷遠，可以柔逋。

translations.literal: It can embrace the distant and soften those who keep their distance.
translations.idiomatic: It can win the distant and soften those afar.

sentences.zh: 如風靡草，威服九區。

translations.literal: Like wind over grass, awe subdues the nine regions.
translations.idiomatic: Like wind over grass, it brings the nine regions to heel.

sentences.zh: 」世甚珍之。

translations.literal: The age greatly treasured them.
translations.idiomatic: The age treasured them greatly.

sentences.zh: 復鑄銅為大鼓，飛廉、翁仲、銅駝、龍獸之屬，皆以黃金飾之，列於宮殿之前。

translations.literal: He also cast bronze into great drums, and Flying Li, Weng Zhong, bronze camels, dragon beasts, and the like—all were adorned with gold and arrayed before the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: He cast great bronze drums and statues of Flying Li, Weng Zhong, camels, and dragons, all gilded and set before the palaces.

sentences.zh: 凡殺工匠數千，以是器物莫不精麗。

translations.literal: In all several thousand craftsmen were killed; therefore every vessel and object was without peer in refinement and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of craftsmen were killed in the process; every object he made was surpassingly fine.

sentences.zh: 於是議討乞伏熾磐。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deliberated attacking Qifu Chipan.
translations.idiomatic: They then debated attacking Qifu Chipan.

sentences.zh: 王買德諫曰：「明王之行師也，軌物以德，不以暴。

translations.literal: Wang Maide remonstrated: "When an enlightened king moves his army, he measures things by virtue and does not rely on violence."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maide remonstrated: "An enlightened king wages war by virtue, not by violence."

sentences.zh: 且熾磐我之與國，新遭大喪，今若伐之，豈所謂乘理而動，上感靈和之義乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Chipan is our allied state and has newly suffered a great bereavement—if we attack now, how is this called acting in accord with reason and moving above with the meaning of spiritual harmony!"
translations.idiomatic: Chipan is our ally and has just lost his father—if we attack now, how is that acting in accord with heaven's harmony?"

sentences.zh: 苟恃眾力，因人喪難，匹夫猶恥為之，而況萬乘哉！

translations.literal: If you rely on the host's strength and take advantage of another's bereavement hardship, even a common man would be ashamed to do it—how much more a lord of ten thousand chariots!"
translations.idiomatic: To prey on another's mourning—even a common man would be ashamed; how much more a Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」勃勃曰：「甚善。

translations.literal: Bobo said: "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Bobo said: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 微卿，朕安聞此言！」

translations.literal: Without you, my lord, how would I have heard these words!"
translations.idiomatic: Without you, how would I have heard this!"

sentences.zh: 其年，下書曰：「朕之皇祖，自北遷幽、朔，姓改姒氏，音殊中國，故從母氏為劉。

translations.literal: That year he issued a document: "My august ancestor, moving north from You and Shuo, changed his surname to Si; the sound differed from China, and therefore he took his mother's surname Liu."
translations.idiomatic: That year he decreed: "My ancestor, moving north from You and Shuo, took the surname Si; the sound differed from China, so he took his mother's surname Liu."

sentences.zh: 子而從母之姓，非禮也。

translations.literal: A son following his mother's surname is not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For a son to bear his mother's surname is not proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 古人氏族無常，或以因生為氏，或以王父之名。

translations.literal: In antiquity clans and surnames were not fixed; some took the name from what they were born to, some from the grandfather-king's name.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient clans took names from birth or from royal forebears.

sentences.zh: 朕將以義易之。

translations.literal: I shall change it according to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: I shall change it as righteousness requires.

sentences.zh: 帝王者，系天為子，是為徽赫實與天連，今改姓曰赫連氏，庶協皇天之意，永享無疆大慶。

translations.literal: The emperor-king is tied to Heaven as son; this is splendor and greatness truly joined with Heaven; now I change my surname to Helian, hoping to accord with Heaven's intent and eternally enjoy boundless great celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is heaven's son, joined to the sky; I change my surname to Helian to accord with heaven and enjoy endless blessing.

sentences.zh: 系天之尊，不可令支庶同之，其非正統，皆以鐵伐為氏，庶朕宗族子孫剛銳如鐵，皆堪伐人。

translations.literal: The honor tied to Heaven may not let collateral branches share it; those not of the legitimate line all take the surname Tieba, hoping my clan's sons and grandsons will be sharp as iron and all able to smite men.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's honor cannot be shared with collateral lines; illegitimate branches take the surname Tieba, that my clan may be sharp as iron and smite all foes.

sentences.zh: 」立其妻梁氏為王后，子璝為太子，封子延陽平公，昌太原公，倫酒泉公，定平原公，滿河南公，安中山公。

translations.literal: He installed his wife Lady Liang as queen, his son Gui as crown prince, enfeoffed his son Yan as Duke of Pingyang, Chang as Duke of Taiyuan, Lun as Duke of Jiuquan, Ding as Duke of Pingyuan, Man as Duke of Henan, and An as Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Lady Liang queen, his son Gui crown prince, and enfeoffed Yan, Chang, Lun, Ding, Man, and An as dukes.

sentences.zh: 又攻姚興將姚逵於杏城，二旬，克之，執逵及其將姚大用、姚安和、姚利僕、尹敵等，坑戰士二萬人。

translations.literal: He again attacked Yao Xing's general Yao Kui at Xingcheng; in twenty days he took it, seized Kui and his generals Yao Dayong, Yao Anhe, Yao Lipu, Yin Di, and the others, and buried alive twenty thousand warriors.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yao Xing's general Yao Kui at Xingcheng, took it in twenty days, seized Kui and his officers, and buried twenty thousand soldiers alive.

sentences.zh: 遣其御史中丞烏洛孤盟于沮渠蒙遜曰：「自金晉數終，禍纏九服，趙、魏為長蛇之墟，秦、隴為豺狼之穴，二都神京，鞠為茂草，蠢爾群生，罔知憑賴。

translations.literal: He sent his Attendant Censor Zhongcheng Wuluo Gu to ally with Juqu Mengxun, saying: "Since Jin ended in number, calamity entwined the nine domains; Zhao and Wei became the lairs of long serpents, Qin and Long the dens of wolves and dogs; the two capitals, divine capitals, were trampled to lush grass, and the mass of living creatures knew nothing to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wuluo Gu to ally with Juqu Mengxun: "Since Jin's fall, calamity has engulfed the realm; the two capitals lie in weeds and the people have nowhere to turn."

sentences.zh: 上天悔禍，運屬二家，封疆密邇，道會義親，宜敦和好，弘康世難。

translations.literal: Heaven repents of calamity and fortune belongs to our two houses; our borders adjoin and our Ways meet in righteous kinship—we should deepen good relations and extend peace through worldly hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven repents; fortune unites our houses. Our borders meet and our Ways align—we should be allies in hardship."

sentences.zh: 爰自終古，有國有家，非盟誓無以昭神祇之心，非斷金無以定終始之好。

translations.literal: From utmost antiquity, whoever had a state or family—without alliance oaths could not manifest the hearts of spirits, without severed gold could not fix friendship to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, states need oaths to bind the spirits and severed gold to seal eternal friendship."

sentences.zh: 然晉、楚之成，吳、蜀之約，咸口血未乾，而尋背之。

translations.literal: Yet the agreements of Jin and Chu, the pacts of Wu and Shu—their mouth-blood was not yet dry before they turned their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin and Chu, Wu and Shu broke their oaths before the blood was dry."

sentences.zh: 今我二家，契殊曩日，言未發而有篤愛之心，音一交而懷傾蓋之顧，息風塵之警，同克濟之誠，戮力一心，共濟六合。

translations.literal: Now our two houses, our bond unlike former days—before words were spoken there was a sincere loving heart; one exchange of sound and there was the regard of leaning-roof friendship; we still the alarm of wind and dust and share the sincerity of overcoming together, unite strength in one heart, and together ford the six harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: Our bond unlike old days: before a word was spoken we felt kinship; one meeting brought trust. Let us still the dust of war and ford the realm together."

sentences.zh: 若天下有事，則雙振義旗；

translations.literal: If the realm has affairs, then both raise the banner of righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: If trouble comes, both raise the banner of righteousness;

sentences.zh: 區域既清，則並敦魯、衛。

translations.literal: when the regions are clear, then together honor Lu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: when peace returns, honor Lu and Wei together."

sentences.zh: 夷險相赴，交易有無，爰及子孫，永崇斯好。

translations.literal: Through ease and peril we answer each other, trade what we lack, reaching to sons and grandsons, eternally honoring this bond.
translations.idiomatic: Through ease and peril we aid each other, trade goods, and bind our descendants to this bond forever."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜遣其將沮渠漢平來盟。

translations.literal: Mengxun sent his general Juqu Hanping to ally.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent his general Juqu Hanping to seal the alliance.

sentences.zh: 勃勃聞姚泓將姚嵩與氐王楊盛相持，率騎四萬襲上邽，未至而嵩為盛所殺。

translations.literal: Bobo heard that Yao Hong's general Yao Song was locked in struggle with the Di king Yang Sheng; he led forty thousand horsemen to raid Shanggui, but before he arrived Song was killed by Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Yao Hong's general Yao Song fought the Di king Yang Sheng, Bobo led forty thousand horse to raid Shanggui; Song was killed before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 勃勃攻上邽，二旬克之，殺泓秦州剌史姚平都及將士五千人，毀城而去。

translations.literal: Bobo attacked Shanggui; in twenty days he took it, killed Hong's Qin Province governor Yao Pingdu and more than five thousand officers and soldiers, destroyed the city, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo took Shanggui in twenty days, killed Governor Yao Pingdu and five thousand men, razed the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進攻陰密，又殺興將姚良子及將士萬餘人。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Yinmi and again killed Xing's general Yao Liangzi and more than ten thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yinmi and killed Yao Liangzi and more than ten thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 以其子昌為使持節、前將軍、雍州刺史，鎮陰密。

translations.literal: He made his son Chang Bearer of the Staff, Forward General, and Governor of Yong Province, garrisoning Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: He made his son Chang forward general and governor of Yong, garrisoning Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 泓將姚恢棄安定，奔于長安，安定人胡儼、華韜率戶五萬據安定，降於勃勃。

translations.literal: Hong's general Yao Hui abandoned Anding and fled to Chang'an; the men of Anding, Hu Yan and Hua Tao, led fifty thousand households to hold Anding and surrender to Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui abandoned Anding for Chang'an; Hu Yan and Hua Tao held Anding with fifty thousand households and surrendered to Bobo.

sentences.zh: 以儼為侍中，韜為尚書，留鎮東羊苟兒鎮之，配以鮮卑五千。

translations.literal: He made Yan Attendant-in-Ordinary and Tao Minister of Works, left Yang Gou'er of the east to garrison it, and assigned five thousand Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: He made Yan attendant and Tao minister of works, left Yang Gou'er to garrison Anding with five thousand Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 進攻泓將姚諶於雍城，諶奔長安。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Hong's general Yao Chen at Yongcheng; Chen fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yao Chen at Yongcheng; Chen fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 勃勃進師次郿城，泓遣其將姚紹來距，勃勃退如安定。

translations.literal: Bobo advanced and encamped at Mei; Hong sent his general Yao Shao to resist; Bobo withdrew toward Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo encamped at Mei; Hong sent Yao Shao against him; Bobo withdrew to Anding.

sentences.zh: 胡儼等襲殺苟兒，以城降泓。

translations.literal: Hu Yan and the others raided and killed Gou'er, surrendering the city to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yan killed Gou'er and surrendered the city to Hong.

sentences.zh: 勃勃引歸杏城，笑謂群臣曰：「劉裕伐秦，水陸兼進，且裕有高世之略，姚泓豈能自固！

translations.literal: Bobo withdrew to Xingcheng and said to his ministers with a laugh: "Liu Yu attacks Qin by land and water together, and Yu has stratagems transcending the age—how can Yao Hong hold firm by himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Bobo withdrew to Xingcheng and laughed: "Liu Yu attacks Qin by land and sea with stratagems beyond his age—how can Yao Hong stand alone?"

sentences.zh: 吾驗以天時人事，必當克之。

translations.literal: I test it by heaven's seasons and human affairs—he is sure to conquer.
translations.idiomatic: By heaven's signs and human affairs he is sure to win.

sentences.zh: 又其兄弟內叛，安可以距人！

translations.literal: Moreover his brothers rebel within—how can he resist others!"
translations.idiomatic: His brothers rebel within—how can he resist outsiders?"

sentences.zh: 裕既克長安，利在速返，正可留子弟及諸將守關中。

translations.literal: When Yu has taken Chang'an, his profit lies in swift return; he can only leave sons and younger brothers and the generals to hold Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu takes Chang'an he will hurry home, leaving only sons and generals to hold Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 待裕發軫，吾取之若拾芥耳，不足復勞吾士馬。

translations.literal: Wait until Yu sets out and I shall take it like picking up a mustard stalk—no need again to weary my officers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu departs I shall take it like picking up a mustard seed—no need to weary my army."

sentences.zh: 」於是秣馬厲兵，休養士卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fed horses and sharpened weapons, resting and nurturing officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He fed horses, sharpened weapons, and rested his troops.

sentences.zh: 尋進據安定，姚泓嶺北鎮戍郡縣悉降，勃勃於是盡有嶺北之地。

translations.literal: Presently he advanced and held Anding; Yao Hong's garrison commanderies and counties north of the mountains all surrendered, and Bobo thereupon fully possessed the lands north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Anding; Hong's garrisons north of the mountains all surrendered, and Bobo held the north.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉裕滅泓，入于長安，遣使遺勃勃書，請通和好，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Yu destroyed Hong and entered Chang'an; he sent envoys with a letter to Bobo requesting good relations and covenanting as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu destroyed Hong, entered Chang'an, and sent envoys proposing brotherhood with Bobo.

sentences.zh: 勃勃命其中書侍郎皇甫徽為文而陰誦之，召裕使前，口授舍人為書，封以答裕。

translations.literal: Bobo ordered his Palace Secretariat Attendant Huangfu Hui to compose a text and memorize it secretly; he summoned Yu forward, dictated it orally to his document clerk to write, sealed it, and returned it to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo had Huangfu Hui compose a reply in secret, then dictated it to a clerk before Liu Yu—who marveled at the text.

sentences.zh: 裕覽其文而奇之，使者又言勃勃容儀瑰偉，英武絕人。

translations.literal: Yu read the text and marveled at it; the envoy also said Bobo's bearing was magnificent and his martial prowess unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Yu read the letter and marveled; the envoy said Bobo's bearing was magnificent and his valor unmatched.

sentences.zh: 裕歎曰：「吾所不如也！

translations.literal: Yu sighed and said: "I am not his equal!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu sighed: "I am not his equal!"

sentences.zh: 」既而勃勃還統萬，裕留子義真鎮長安而還。

translations.literal: Presently Bobo returned to Tongwan; Yu left his son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo returned to Tongwan; Yu left his son Yizhen at Chang'an and went home.

sentences.zh: 勃勃聞之，大悅，謂王買德曰：「朕將進圖長安，卿試言取之方略。

translations.literal: When Bobo heard this he was greatly pleased and said to Wang Maide: "I shall advance to take Chang'an—try to speak the strategy for taking it."
translations.idiomatic: Bobo was delighted and asked Wang Maide: "I mean to take Chang'an—tell me how."

sentences.zh: 」買德曰：「劉裕滅秦，所謂以亂平亂，未有德政以濟蒼生。

translations.literal: Maide said: "Liu Yu destroyed Qin—what is called using disorder to pacify disorder; there is no virtuous government to aid the black-haired masses."
translations.idiomatic: Maide said: "Liu Yu ended Qin by disorder, not by virtue—the people have no relief."

sentences.zh: 關中形勝之地，而以弱才小兒守之，非經遠之規也。

translations.literal: Guanzhong is terrain of strategic advantage, yet a weak talent and small child guard it—not a plan reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is strategic ground, guarded by a weak boy—not a far-sighted plan.

sentences.zh: 狼狽而返者，欲速成篡事耳，無暇有意于中原。

translations.literal: He returns in distress because he wishes to hurry the matter of usurpation and has no leisure to care for the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: He hurries home to usurp the throne and has no time for the central plains.

sentences.zh: 陛下以順伐逆，義貫幽顯，百姓以君命望陛下義旗之至，以日為歲矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with obedience attacks rebellion, righteousness penetrating the hidden and manifest; the hundred surnames await Your Majesty's banner of righteous army as if counting days by years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attacks rebellion with justice; the people have awaited your banner for years.

sentences.zh: 青泥、上洛，南師之沖要，宜置遊兵斷其去來之路。

translations.literal: Qingni and Shangluo are the vital passes of the southern army—you should set roaming troops to cut their coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Qingni and Shangluo are the southern army's vital passes—set roaming troops to cut their retreat.

sentences.zh: 然後杜潼關，塞崤、陝，絕其水陸之道。

translations.literal: Then block Tong Pass, seal Xiao and Shan, and cut their water and land roads.
translations.idiomatic: Then block Tong Pass and Xiao and Shan and cut their roads by land and water.

sentences.zh: 陛下聲檄長安，申布恩澤，三輔父老皆壺漿以迎王師矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's proclamation at Chang'an, spreading grace— the elders of the three auxiliaries will all bring wine and broth to welcome the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim grace at Chang'an and the three auxiliaries will welcome you with wine.

sentences.zh: 義真獨坐空城，逃竄無所，一旬之間必面縛麾下，所謂兵不血刃，不戰而自定也。

translations.literal: Yizhen sits alone in an empty city with nowhere to flee; within ten days he is sure to bind himself before your majesty's horse—what is called arms without bloody blades, settled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen sits in an empty city with nowhere to flee; within ten days he will bind himself before you—arms without blood, victory without battle.

sentences.zh: 」勃勃善之，以子璝都督前鋒諸軍事，領撫軍大將軍，率騎二萬南伐長安，前將軍赫連昌屯兵潼關，以買德為撫軍右長史，南斷青泥，勃勃率大軍繼發。

translations.literal: Bobo approved; he made his son Gui commander of the vanguard armies, Pacification Grand General, leading twenty thousand horse south to attack Chang'an; the Forward General Helian Chang encamped at Tong Pass; Maide was made Pacification Right Chief Clerk to cut Qingni in the south; Bobo followed with the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo approved: Gui led twenty thousand horse on Chang'an, Chang held Tong Pass, Maide blocked Qingni, and Bobo followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 璝至渭陽，降者屬路。

translations.literal: Gui reached Weiyang; those who surrendered lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Gui reached Weiyang; surrenderers lined the road.

sentences.zh: 義真遣龍驤將軍沈田子率眾逆戰，不利而退，屯劉回堡。

translations.literal: Yizhen sent the Flying Cavalry General Shen Tianzi to lead the host to meet in battle; he was unsuccessful and withdrew, encamping at Liuhui Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen sent Shen Tianzi against him; Tianzi was beaten back to Liuhui Fort.

sentences.zh: 田子與義真司馬王鎮惡不平，因鎮惡出城，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Tianzi and Yizhen's Marshal Wang Zhen'e were at odds; because Zhen'e left the city, Tianzi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi quarreled with Yizhen's marshal Wang Zhen'e and killed him when he left the city.

sentences.zh: 義真又殺田子。

translations.literal: Yizhen also killed Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen then killed Tianzi.

sentences.zh: 於是悉召外軍入於城中，閉門距守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all external armies into the city, shut the gates, and held in defense.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled all outside troops, shut the gates, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 關中郡縣悉降。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties of Guanzhong all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong's commanderies and counties surrendered.

sentences.zh: 璝夜襲長安，不克。

translations.literal: Gui raided Chang'an by night and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui raided Chang'an by night and failed.

sentences.zh: 勃勃進據咸陽，長安樵采路絕。

translations.literal: Bobo advanced and held Xianyang; the fuel-gathering roads of Chang'an were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo took Xianyang; Chang'an's supply roads were cut.

sentences.zh: 劉裕聞之，大懼，乃召義真東鎮洛陽，以硃齡石為雍州刺史，守長安。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu heard he was greatly afraid; he summoned Yizhen east to garrison Luoyang and made Zhu Lingshi Governor of Yong to hold Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu in alarm recalled Yizhen to Luoyang and sent Zhu Lingshi to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 義真大掠而東，至於灞上，百姓遂逐齡石，而迎勃勃入于長安。

translations.literal: Yizhen plundered greatly as he went east; when he reached Bashang the common people drove out Lingshi and welcomed Bobo into Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen plundered as he fled east; at Bashang the people expelled Lingshi and welcomed Bobo into Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 璝率眾三萬追擊義真，王師敗績，義真單馬而遁。

translations.literal: Gui led thirty thousand to pursue Yizhen; the royal army was defeated and Yizhen fled on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pursued Yizhen with thirty thousand; the Jin army was routed and Yizhen escaped alone.

sentences.zh: 買德獲晉甯朔將軍傅弘之、輔國將軍蒯恩、義真司馬毛脩之於青泥，積人頭以為京觀。

translations.literal: Maide captured the Jin General of Pacifying the North Fu Hongzhi, the Pacification General Kuai En, and Yizhen's Marshal Mao Xiuzhi at Qingni and piled heads into a mound.
translations.idiomatic: Maide captured Fu Hongzhi, Kuai En, and Mao Xiuzhi at Qingni and piled their heads into a mound.

sentences.zh: 於是勃勃大饗將士于長安，舉觴謂王買德曰：「卿往日之言，一周而果效，可謂算無遺策矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bobo held a great feast for officers at Chang'an, raised his cup and said to Wang Maide: "Your words of other days bore fruit within a week—one may call it a plan without leftover strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Bobo feasted his officers in Chang'an and told Maide: "Your words bore fruit within a week—no strategy left over."

sentences.zh: 雖宗廟社稷之靈，亦卿謀獻之力也。

translations.literal: Though the spirits of the ancestral temple and altars also had your plotting contribution.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral spirits helped—but so did your counsel.

sentences.zh: 此觴所集，非卿而誰！

translations.literal: This cup gathers—not you, who else!"
translations.idiomatic: This cup is for you alone!"

sentences.zh: 」於是拜買德都官尚書，加冠軍將軍，封河陽侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Maide Director of the Masters of Writing, added Champion General, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He made Maide director of the masters of writing, champion general, and marquis of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 赫連昌攻齡石及龍驤將軍王敬于潼關之曹公故壘，克之，執齡石及敬送于長安。

translations.literal: Helian Chang attacked Lingshi and the Flying Cavalry General Wang Jing at Cao Gong's old rampart on Tong Pass, took it, seized Lingshi and Jing, and sent them to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang took Tong Pass, seized Zhu Lingshi and Wang Jing, and sent them to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 群臣乃勸進，勃勃曰：「朕無撥亂之才，不能弘濟兆庶，自枕戈寢甲，十有二年，而四海未同，遺寇尚熾，不知何以謝責當年，垂之來葉！

translations.literal: The ministers thereupon urged him to advance; Bobo said: "I have no talent for settling disorder and cannot broadly aid the masses; since I lay on my spear and slept in my armor for twelve years, the four seas are not united and remnant enemies still burn—I do not know how to answer for my blame to the age or hand it down to later generations!"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged him to take the throne; Bobo said: "I have no talent to save the realm; twelve years at war and enemies still burn—how can I face posterity?"

sentences.zh: 將明揚仄陋，以王位讓之，然後歸老朔方，琴書卒歲。

translations.literal: I shall make known and raise the obscure and lowly, yield the royal position to them, then return old to Shuofang and end my years with zither and book.
translations.idiomatic: I shall find a worthy man, yield the throne, and retire to Shuofang with zither and books.

sentences.zh: 皇帝之號，豈薄德所膺！

translations.literal: The title of emperor—how can shallow virtue bear it!"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial title—how can my shallow virtue bear it!"

sentences.zh: 」群臣固請，乃許之。

translations.literal: The ministers firmly requested and he thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed him and he consented.

sentences.zh: 於是為壇於灞上，僭即皇帝位，赦其境內，改元為昌武。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made an altar at Bashang, usurped the emperor's position, amnestied within the borders, and changed the era name to Changwu.
translations.idiomatic: He made an altar at Bashang, took the throne, amnestied the realm, and proclaimed the Changwu era.

sentences.zh: 遣其將叱奴侯提率步騎二萬攻晉并州刺史毛德祖于蒲阪，德祖奔於洛陽。

translations.literal: He sent his general Chinu Houti with twenty thousand foot and horse to attack Jin's Bing Province governor Mao Dezu at Puban; Dezu fled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chinu Houti with twenty thousand men against Mao Dezu at Puban; Dezu fled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以侯提為并州刺史，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: He made Houti Governor of Bing and garrisoned Puban.
translations.idiomatic: He made Houti governor of Bing and garrisoned Puban.

sentences.zh: 勃勃歸於長安，征隱士京兆韋祖思。

translations.literal: Bobo returned to Chang'an and summoned the recluse of Jingzhao, Wei Zusi.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo returned to Chang'an and summoned the recluse Wei Zusi of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 既至而恭懼過禮，勃勃怒曰：「吾以國士征汝，柰何以非類處吾！

translations.literal: When he arrived he was overly respectful in ceremony; Bobo in anger said: "I summoned you as a scholar of the state—how can you treat me as a non-human!"
translations.idiomatic: Zusi was overly deferential; Bobo raged: "I summoned a national scholar—why treat me as less than human!"

sentences.zh: 汝昔不拜姚興，何獨拜我？

translations.literal: You formerly did not bow to Yao Xing—why alone bow to me?
translations.idiomatic: You would not bow to Yao Xing—why bow to me?

sentences.zh: 我今未死，汝猶不以我為帝王，吾死之後，汝輩弄筆，當置吾何地！

translations.literal: I am not yet dead—you still do not take me for an emperor-king; after I die, you lot will wield the brush—where will you place me!"
translations.idiomatic: I am not dead yet you deny me an emperor; when I die you will write history—where will you put me!"

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He killed him.

sentences.zh: 群臣勸都長安，勃勃曰：「朕豈不知長安累帝舊都，有山河四塞之固！

translations.literal: The ministers urged making Chang'an the capital; Bobo said: "Do I not know Chang'an was the old capital of successive emperors, with mountains and rivers and four passes as fortification!"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged Chang'an as capital; Bobo said: "I know Chang'an was the emperors' old capital, fortified by mountains and rivers!"

sentences.zh: 但荊、吳僻遠，勢不能為人之患。

translations.literal: But Jing and Wu are remote and cannot become men's worry.
translations.idiomatic: But Jing and Wu are far and pose no threat.

sentences.zh: 東魏與我同壤境，去北京裁數百餘里，若都長安，北京恐有不守之憂。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei shares our border soil; going north from there is only several hundred li—if we capital at Chang'an, I fear Beijing will have the worry of not being held.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei borders us only hundreds of li north—if we capital at Chang'an, the northern capital may not hold.

sentences.zh: 朕在統萬，彼終不敢濟河，諸卿適未見此耳！

translations.literal: I at Tongwan—they in the end will not dare cross the river; you lords have simply not seen this!"
translations.idiomatic: At Tongwan they will never dare cross the river—you have not seen this!"

sentences.zh: 」其下咸曰：「非所及也。

translations.literal: Those below all said: "Beyond what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: All said: "Beyond our understanding."

sentences.zh: 」乃于長安置南台，以璝領大將軍、雍州牧、錄南台尚書事。

translations.literal: He thereupon set up the Southern Terrace at Chang'an, made Gui Grand General, Governor of Yong, and Director of the Southern Terrace Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He set up the Southern Terrace at Chang'an and made Gui grand general, governor of Yong, and director of its secretariat.

sentences.zh: 勃勃還統萬，以宮殿大成，於是赦其境內，又改元曰真興。

translations.literal: Bobo returned to Tongwan; because the palaces were completed, he amnestied within the borders and again changed the era name to Zhenxing.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo returned to Tongwan; the palaces complete, he amnestied the realm and proclaimed the Zhenxing era.

sentences.zh: 刻石都南，頌其功德，曰：

translations.literal: He carved stone south of the capital, praising his merit and virtue, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He carved stone south of the capital to praise his merit, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫庸大德盛者，必建不刊之業；

translations.literal: Those of great virtue and abundant merit surely establish enterprises that cannot be effaced;
translations.idiomatic: Men of great virtue and merit establish imperishable achievements;

sentences.zh: 道積慶隆者，必享無窮之祚。

translations.literal: those whose Way accumulates and blessing flourishes surely enjoy boundless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: those whose Way accumulates and blessing endures enjoy fortune without end.

sentences.zh: 昔在陶唐，數鐘厄運，我皇祖大禹以至聖之姿，當經綸之會，鑿龍門面辟伊闕，疏三江而決九河，夷一元之窮災，拯六合之沈溺，鴻績侔於天地，神功邁於造化，故二儀降祉，三靈葉贊，揖讓受終，光啟有夏。

translations.literal: Of old under Potao Tang, number struck adverse fortune; our august ancestor Great Yu with utmost sage bearing met the age of ordering the realm, opened Dragon Gate and faced Yi Que, cleared the three rivers and cut the nine streams, quelled the utmost calamity of the One Origin, and rescued the drowning of the six harmonies—his great achievement matched Heaven and Earth, his divine merit surpassed creation; therefore the two regulators sent blessing, the three spirits joined in praise, he yielded and received the end, and brightly opened the age of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao, fortune turned adverse; our ancestor Yu with sage bearing ordered the realm, opened Dragon Gate, cleared the rivers, and saved the world—his merit matched heaven and earth, the two regulators blessed him, and he founded Xia.

sentences.zh: 傳世二十，曆載四百，賢辟相承，哲王繼軌，徽猷冠于玄古，高範煥乎疇昔。

translations.literal: Twenty generations passed down, four hundred years recorded, worthy successors followed, sage kings continued the track—eminent principles crowned remote antiquity, lofty models shone in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty generations, four hundred years—worthy heirs and sage kings carried on, their principles crowning antiquity and their models shining through former ages.

sentences.zh: 而道無常夷，數或屯險，王桀不綱，網漏殷氏，用使金暉絕于中天，神轡輟于促路。

translations.literal: Yet the Way has no constant peace and number sometimes meets hardship; the king of Jie lost the guiding rope, the net leaked the Yin house, and the golden splendor was cut off at mid-heaven, the divine chariot halted on the short road.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Way knows no constant peace: Jie lost the thread of rule, Yin's net broke, and golden splendor failed at mid-heaven.

sentences.zh: 然純曜未渝，慶綿萬祀，龍飛漠南，鳳峙朔北。

translations.literal: Yet pure radiance was not changed and blessing extended through ten thousand sacrifices; the dragon flew south of the desert, the phoenix stood north of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pure radiance endured and blessing ran ten thousand generations; the dragon flew beyond the desert, the phoenix stood in the northern wilds.

sentences.zh: 長轡遠馭，則西罩昆山之外；

translations.literal: With long reins driving far, then the west covered beyond Kunshan;
translations.idiomatic: Driving far on long reins, the west reached beyond Kunshan;

sentences.zh: 密網遐張，則東亙滄海之表。

translations.literal: with close nets spread afar, then the east reached across the blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: casting nets afar, the east reached the blue sea.

sentences.zh: 爰始逮今，二千餘載，雖三統迭制於崤、函，五德革運于伊、洛，秦、雍成篡殺之墟，周、豫為爭奪之藪，而幽朔謐爾，主有常尊於上；

translations.literal: From beginning to now, more than two thousand years—though the three successions in turn ruled at Xiao and Han, the five virtues changed fortune at Yi and Luo, Qin and Yong became ruins of usurpation and slaughter, Zhou and Yu became marshes of contention, yet You and Shuo were tranquil and the lord had constant honor above;
translations.idiomatic: For two thousand years, though dynasties rose at Xiao and Han and Qin and Yong became battlegrounds, the north stayed calm and the lord kept his throne.

sentences.zh: 海代晏然，物無異望於下。

translations.literal: the sea frontiers were peaceful and things had no different hope below.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was peaceful and the people knew no other master.

sentences.zh: 故能控弦之眾百有餘萬，躍馬長驅，鼓行秦、趙，使中原疲於奔命，諸夏不得高枕，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the host who could bend the bow numbered more than a million; leaping horses and long drives, drumming advance through Qin and Zhao, they made the central plains weary with urgent orders and the many Xia could not rest their heads high—for long indeed.
translations.idiomatic: A million bowmen rode through Qin and Zhao, wearing the central plains to exhaustion for ages.

sentences.zh: 是以偏師暫擬，涇陽摧隆周之鋒；

translations.literal: Therefore a partial division for a time matched the blade of elevated Zhou at Jingyang;
translations.idiomatic: A partial force once blunted Zhou's edge at Jingyang;

sentences.zh: 赫斯一奮，平陽挫漢祖之銳。

translations.literal: one fierce burst flattened the sharpness of Han's ancestor at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: one fierce charge broke Han's ancestor at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 雖霸王繼蹤，猶朝日之升扶桑；

translations.literal: Though overlords and hegemons followed in track, they were like the morning sun rising over Fusang;
translations.idiomatic: Though hegemons followed, they were like the morning sun over Fusang;

sentences.zh: 英豪接踵，若夕月之登濛汜。

translations.literal: heroes and outstanding men succeeded one another, like the evening moon mounting Mengsi.
translations.idiomatic: heroes came in succession like the evening moon over Mengsi.

sentences.zh: 自開闢已來，未始聞也。

translations.literal: From opening the age until now, it has not been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Since the world's beginning, nothing like it was heard.

sentences.zh: 非夫卜世與乾坤比長，鴻基與山嶽齊固，孰能本枝于千葉，重光于萬祀，履寒霜而逾榮，蒙重氛而彌耀者哉！

translations.literal: Unless one's allotted generations compare in length with heaven and earth, the great foundation with mountains and hills in solidity—who could branch through a thousand leaves, double radiance through ten thousand sacrifices, tread cold frost and grow more glorious, bear heavy miasma and shine the more!
translations.idiomatic: Unless fortune matches heaven and earth and the foundation mountains—who could flourish through a thousand branches, grow brighter through frost, and shine through miasma!

sentences.zh: 於是玄符告征，大猷有會，我皇誕命世之期，應天縱之運，仰協時來，俯順時望。

translations.literal: Thereupon the dark talisman announced the expedition, the great plan had its meeting; our emperor was born to the age's term, answered heaven's unrestrained fortune, looked up to harmonize with the coming season, bowed down to follow the age's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Then heaven's sign appeared; our emperor was born to his age, answered heaven's mandate, and harmonized with the people's hope.

sentences.zh: 龍升北京，則義風蓋于九區；

translations.literal: The dragon rose in northern Beijing, then righteous wind covered the nine districts;
translations.idiomatic: The dragon rose in the northern capital and righteous wind covered the realm;

sentences.zh: 鳳翔天域，則威聲格於八表。

translations.literal: the phoenix soared in heaven's domain, then awesome sound reached the eight borders.
translations.idiomatic: the phoenix soared in heaven's realm and awe reached the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 屬奸雄鼎峙之秋，群凶嶽立之際，昧旦臨朝，日旰忘膳，運籌命將，舉無遺策。

translations.literal: It fell in the season when treacherous heroes stood like tripods and many villains rose like peaks; he attended court before dawn and forgot meals at sundown, strategized and commanded generals, and in raising there was no leftover plan.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of rival warlords he held court from dawn to dusk, strategized without waste, and commanded without error.

sentences.zh: 親禦六戎，則有征無戰。

translations.literal: Personally he led the six armies and there was expedition without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He led the six armies in person and conquered without fighting.

sentences.zh: 故偽秦以三世之資，喪魂于關、隴；

translations.literal: Therefore the false Qin with three generations' resources lost its soul at Guan and Long;
translations.idiomatic: False Qin with three generations' wealth lost heart at Guan and Long;

sentences.zh: 河源望旗而委質，北虜欽風而納款。

translations.literal: the River Source watched the banners and submitted, the northern barbarians admired the wind and offered allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: the River Source submitted at his banners, northern tribes offered allegiance to his wind.

sentences.zh: 德音著於柔服，威刑彰於伐叛，文教與武功並宣，俎豆與干戈俱運。

translations.literal: Virtuous sound showed in gentle submission, martial punishment showed in punishing rebellion; civil teaching and martial achievement were both proclaimed, meat stands and weapons both deployed.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue won the gentle, arms punished rebels; civil and martial teaching spread together.

sentences.zh: 五稔之間，道風弘著，暨乎七載而王猷允洽。

translations.literal: Within five harvests the Way's wind was greatly displayed; reaching seven years the king's plan was fully harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years his Way shone; in seven his rule was complete.

sentences.zh: 乃遠惟周文，啟經始之基；

translations.literal: He looked far to King Wen of Zhou, opening the foundation of beginning;
translations.idiomatic: He looked to King Wen of Zhou for the foundation of rule;

sentences.zh: 近詳山川，究形勝之地，遂營起都城，開建京邑。

translations.literal: he examined near the mountains and rivers, investigating terrain of strategic advantage; thereupon he raised the capital city and opened the imperial metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: he studied mountains and rivers and founded the capital.

sentences.zh: 背名山而面洪流，左河津而右重塞。

translations.literal: Backed by famous mountains and facing rushing floods, the Yellow River ford on the left and layered passes on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by mountains, facing floods, with the Yellow River on the left and layered passes on the right.

sentences.zh: 高隅隱日，崇墉際雲，石郭天池，周綿千里。

translations.literal: High corners hid the sun, lofty walls met the clouds; stone outer walls and heaven's pool encircled a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: High walls hid the sun and met the clouds; stone ramparts and heaven's pool ran a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其為獨守之形，險絕之狀，固以遠邁於咸陽，超美于周洛，若乃廣五郊之義，尊七廟之制，崇左社之規，建右稷之禮，禦太一以繕明堂，模帝坐而營路寢，閶闔披霄而山亭，象魏排虛而岳峙，華林靈沼，崇台秘室，通房連閣，馳道苑園，可以陰映萬邦，光覆四海，莫不鬱然並建，森然畢備，若紫微之帶皇穹，閬風之跨后土。

translations.literal: Its form as sole defense, its aspect of extreme peril, already far surpassed Xianyang and excelled Zhou and Luo; as for extending the meaning of the five suburbs, honoring the seven temples, exalting the left altar's rule, establishing the right grain altar's rites, repairing the Bright Hall to pattern the Grand One, modeling the imperial seat to build the road chamber, Changhe piercing heaven like mountain pavilions, the elephant tower thrusting void like peaks, Flowery Forest and Spirit Pool, lofty terraces and secret chambers, connected rooms and linked pavilions, racing roads and parks—they could shade the ten thousand states below and shine over the four seas; none were not lushly built together, densely complete, like Purple Subtlety girdling the imperial vault, Lang Wind striding the later earth.
translations.idiomatic: Its defenses far surpassed Xianyang and Luoyang: five suburbs, seven temples, Bright Hall, linked towers and racing roads shaded the realm and shone over the seas like stars girdling heaven.

sentences.zh: 然宰司鼎臣，群黎士庶，僉以為重威之式，有闕前王。

translations.literal: Yet the chief ministers and the mass of officials and commoners all held that the form of heavy awe had a lack before former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ministers and people held that his majesty's awe still lacked something before former kings.

sentences.zh: 於是延王爾之奇工，命班輸之妙匠，搜文梓于鄧林，采繡石于恆嶽，九域貢以金銀，八方獻其瑰寶，親運神奇，參制規矩，營離宮於露寢之南，起別殿于永安之北。

translations.literal: Thereupon he extended the marvelous craftsmen of Wang Er, commanded the subtle artisans of Ban Chu, sought patterned catalpa in Deng Forest, gathered embroidered stone on Mount Heng; the nine domains offered gold and silver, the eight directions presented rare treasures; he personally wielded wonder, jointly set compass and square, built a detached palace south of the open chamber and raised a separate hall north of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned master craftsmen, gathered timber and stone from every quarter, and personally directed wonder—building detached palaces south and north of the main halls.

sentences.zh: 高構千尋，崇基萬仞。

translations.literal: High structure a thousand ren, lofty foundation ten thousand ren.
