translations.idiomatic: Structures rose a thousand ren on foundations ten thousand ren deep.

sentences.zh: 玄棟鏤榥，若騰虹之揚眉；

translations.literal: Dark beams carved rafters, like soaring rainbow lifting brows;
translations.idiomatic: Dark beams and carved rafters arched like rainbows;

sentences.zh: 飛簷舒咢，似翔鵬之矯翼。

translations.literal: flying eaves spreading beaks, like soaring peng bending wings.
translations.idiomatic: flying eaves spread like the peng bird's wings.

sentences.zh: 二序啟矣，而五時之坐開；

translations.literal: The two sequences opened and the seats of the five seasons were set;
translations.idiomatic: Two halls opened and seats for the five seasons were set;

sentences.zh: 四隅陳設，而一禦之位建。

translations.literal: the four corners were arrayed and the one imperial seat was established.
translations.idiomatic: four corners were arrayed and the imperial seat established.

sentences.zh: 溫宮膠葛，涼殿崢嶸，絡以隋珠，綷以金鏡，雖曦望互升於表，而中無晝夜之殊；

translations.literal: Warm palaces intertwined, cool halls towering, bound with Sui pearls, adorned with gold mirrors—though dawn and full moon alternately rose outside, within there was no difference of day and night;
translations.idiomatic: Warm and cool halls towered, bound with pearls and mirrors—within, no difference of day or night;

sentences.zh: 陰陽迭更於外，而內無寒暑之別。

translations.literal: yin and yang alternated without, yet within there was no distinction of cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: without, yin and yang changed; within, no cold or heat.

sentences.zh: 故善目者不能為其名，博辯者不能究其稱，斯蓋神明之所規模，非人工之所經制。

translations.literal: Therefore keen-eyed ones could not name it, broad debaters could not exhaust its designation—this was surely what spirits and gods planned, not what human craft could measure.
translations.idiomatic: Keen eyes could not name it, eloquence could not describe it—this was the work of gods, not men.

sentences.zh: 若乃尋名以求類，蹤狀以效真，據質以究名，形疑妙出，雖如來、須彌之寶塔，帝釋、忉利之神宮，尚未足以喻其麗，方其飾矣。

translations.literal: If one seeks the category by name, traces form to test truth, tests substance to investigate name—form in doubt, wonder emerges—though the treasure pagoda of Tathagata and Vajra, the divine palace of Shakra and Trayastrimsa, they are not yet enough to compare its beauty when ornamented.
translations.idiomatic: By name and form it surpassed even the Buddha's pagoda and Indra's palace in splendor.

sentences.zh: 昔周宣考室而詠于詩人，閟宮有侐而頌聲是作。

translations.literal: Of old King Xuan of Zhou examined the chamber and the poets sang; the closed palace had grandeur and eulogy was made.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan of Zhou built his chamber and poets sang; so too this palace called forth praise.

sentences.zh: 況乃太微肇制，清都啟建，軌一文昌，舊章唯始，咸秩百神，賓享萬國，群生開其耳目，天下詠其來蘇，亦何得不播之管弦，刊之金石哉！

translations.literal: How much more when the Grand Subtlety first established rule, the pure capital opened and was built, the track unified Wenchang, old statutes only beginning, all ranks ordering the hundred spirits, ten thousand states guest-feasting—living creatures opened their ears and eyes, the realm sang of returning repose—how could it not be broadcast on pipes and strings, carved in metal and stone!
translations.idiomatic: How much more this founding of the capital, ordering spirits and feasting nations—the realm sang of repose; how could it not be carved in stone and sung on strings!

sentences.zh: 乃樹銘都邑，敷贊碩美，俾皇風振于來葉，聖庸垂乎不朽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set up inscription in the capital, spread praise of great beauty, that imperial wind might shake coming generations and sage merit hang immortal.
translations.idiomatic: He set inscription in the capital that imperial wind might shake coming ages and sage merit endure.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The text says:
translations.idiomatic: The text says:

sentences.zh: 於赫靈祚，配乾比靈斯。

translations.literal: Ah, the numinous fortune, matching Qian, comparing with numinous splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Ah, numinous fortune, matching heaven's splendor.

sentences.zh: 巍巍大禹，堂堂聖功。

translations.literal: Towering Great Yu, hall of sage achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Towering Great Yu, hall of sage achievement.

sentences.zh: 仁被蒼生，德格玄穹。

translations.literal: Benevolence spread to the black-haired masses, virtue reached the dark vault.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence spread to the people, virtue reached heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝錫玄珪，揖讓受終。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed the dark tablet; yielding, he received the end.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven bestowed the dark tablet; he yielded and received the throne.

sentences.zh: 哲王繼軌，光闡徽風。

translations.literal: Sage kings continued the track, brightly opening eminent wind.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings continued the line, opening eminent wind.

sentences.zh: 道無常夷，數或不競。

translations.literal: The Way has no constant peace, number sometimes does not compete.
translations.idiomatic: The Way knows no constant peace; fortune sometimes fails.

sentences.zh: 金精南邁，天輝北映。

translations.literal: Golden essence marched south, heaven's splendor reflected north.
translations.idiomatic: Golden splendor moved south, heaven's light shone north.

sentences.zh: 靈祉逾昌，世葉彌盛。

translations.literal: Numinous blessing grew ever more flourishing, generations of the house more thriving.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing flourished, the house's generations thrived.

sentences.zh: 惟祖惟父，克廣休命。

translations.literal: Forefathers and fathers, broadly extending fine mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Forefathers extended the fine mandate.

sentences.zh: 如彼日月，連光接鏡。

translations.literal: Like sun and moon, joined light, joined mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Like sun and moon, joined in light.

sentences.zh: 玄符瑞德，乾運有歸。

translations.literal: Dark talisman, auspicious virtue, Qian's fortune has return.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sign and auspicious virtue—fortune returns.

sentences.zh: 誕鐘我後，應圖龍飛。

translations.literal: Born ringing our sovereign, answering the chart, dragon flies.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign was born to the chart; the dragon flies.

sentences.zh: 落落神武，恢恢聖姿。

translations.literal: Lofty, lofty divine martial, vast, vast sage bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty divine martial, vast sage bearing.

sentences.zh: 名教內敷，群妖外夷。

translations.literal: Name-teaching spread within, all demons subdued without.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching spread within, demons subdued without.

sentences.zh: 化光四表，威截九圍。

translations.literal: Transforming light to the four tables, awe cutting the nine peripheries.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming light reached the four quarters, his awe the nine borders.

sentences.zh: 封畿之制，王者常經。

translations.literal: The system of the royal domain—kings' constant canon.
translations.idiomatic: The royal domain—kings' constant law.

sentences.zh: 乃延輸、爾，肇建帝京。

translations.literal: Thereupon he extended Shu and Er, first establishing the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned master builders and founded the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 土苞上壤，地跨勝形。

translations.literal: Earth wrapped the upper soil, ground crossed winning form.
translations.idiomatic: Earth embraced the upper realm, ground crossed triumphant terrain.

sentences.zh: 庶人子來，不日而成。

translations.literal: Common men came like sons, completed not in a day.
translations.idiomatic: The people came like sons; it was finished in no day.

sentences.zh: 崇台霄峙，秀闕雲亭。

translations.literal: Lofty terraces pierced heaven, elegant towers touched clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty terraces pierced heaven, elegant towers touched clouds.

sentences.zh: 千榭連隅，萬閣接屏。

translations.literal: A thousand pavilions linked corners, ten thousand towers joined screens.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand pavilions linked corners, ten thousand towers joined screens.

sentences.zh: 晃若晨曦，昭若列星。

translations.literal: Bright as morning dawn, clear as arrayed stars.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as dawn, clear as stars.

sentences.zh: 離宮既作，別宇雲施。

translations.literal: Detached palace already made, separate halls spread like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Detached palaces rose, separate halls spread like clouds.

sentences.zh: 爰構崇明，仰准乾儀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built Chongming, looking up to Qian's model.
translations.idiomatic: He built Chongming, looking up to heaven's model.

sentences.zh: 懸薨風閱，飛軒雲垂。

translations.literal: Suspended rafters wind-passing, flying galleries cloud-hanging.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended rafters passed the wind, flying galleries hung like clouds.

sentences.zh: 溫室嵯峨，層城參差。

translations.literal: Warm chambers lofty, layered walls uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Warm chambers towered, layered walls rose uneven.

sentences.zh: 楹雕虯獸，節鏤龍螭。

translations.literal: Pillars carved with horned beasts, nodes carved with dragon wyrms.
translations.idiomatic: Pillars carved with horned beasts, nodes with dragon wyrms.

sentences.zh: 瑩以寶璞，飾以珍奇。

translations.literal: Gleaming with precious jade, ornamented with rare wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Gleaming with jade, ornamented with wonder.

sentences.zh: 稱因褒著，名由實揚。

translations.literal: Name follows praise of cause, name by substance is raised.
translations.idiomatic: Name follows substance, praise follows merit.

sentences.zh: 偉哉皇室，盛矣厥章！

translations.literal: Great the imperial house, flourishing its chapters!
translations.idiomatic: Great the imperial house, flourishing its glory!

sentences.zh: 義高靈台，美隆未央。

translations.literal: Righteousness high as the Spirit Terrace, beauty grand as Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous as the Spirit Terrace, grand as Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 邁軌三五，貽則霸王。

translations.literal: Surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five, bequeathing models to hegemons and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Surpassing the Three and Five, bequeathing models to kings.

sentences.zh: 永世垂節，億載彌光。

translations.literal: Forever hanging festival through ages, a hundred million years ever bright.
translations.idiomatic: Forever hanging through ages, shining for a hundred million years.

sentences.zh: 其秘書監胡義周之辭也。

translations.literal: This was the text of the Director of the Masters of Writing Hu Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: This was the text of Director of the Masters of Writing Hu Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 名其南門曰朝宋門，東門曰招魏門，西門曰服涼門，北門曰平朔門。

translations.literal: He named the southern gate Gate of Attending Song, the eastern gate Gate of Summoning Wei, the western gate Gate of Serving Liang, the northern gate Gate of Pacifying Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He named the gates: south Attending Song, east Summoning Wei, west Serving Liang, north Pacifying Shuo.

sentences.zh: 追尊其高祖訓兒曰元皇帝，曾祖武曰景皇帝，祖豹子曰宣皇帝，父衛辰曰桓皇帝，廟號太祖，母苻氏曰桓文皇后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather Xun'er as Emperor Yuan, his grandfather Wu as Emperor Jing, his grandfather Baozi as Emperor Xuan, his father Weichen as Emperor Huan, temple name Taizu, and his mother of the Fu clan as Empress Huanwen.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his forebears as emperors Yuan, Jing, Xuan, and Huan, with temple name Taizu, and his mother as Empress Huanwen.

sentences.zh: 勃勃性凶暴好殺，無順守之規。

translations.literal: Bobo by nature was fierce, violent, and fond of killing, without the rule of obedient preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo was by nature fierce, violent, and murderous, without regard for stable rule.

sentences.zh: 常居城上，置弓劍於側，有所嫌忿，便手自殺之，群臣忤視者毀其目，笑者決其脣，諫者謂之誹謗，先截其舌而後斬之。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt atop the city wall, setting bow and sword at his side; when he harbored resentment he personally killed the man; ministers who looked at him askance he destroyed their eyes, those who laughed he cut their lips, those who remonstrated he called slanderers—first cut out the tongue, then behead.
translations.idiomatic: He lived atop the wall with bow and sword at hand; he killed those he resented, gouged the eyes of those who stared, cut the lips of those who laughed, and cut out the tongues of remonstrators before beheading them.

sentences.zh: 夷夏囂然，人無生賴。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Chinese were clamorous; men had no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Chinese alike clamored; men had no way to live.

sentences.zh: 在位十三年而宋受禪，以宋元嘉二年死。

translations.literal: He reigned thirteen years and Song received the mandate; in the second year of Yuanjia of Song he died.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned thirteen years; Song received the mandate; he died in the second year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 子昌嗣偽位，尋為魏所擒。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded to the usurped throne and before long was captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded him and was soon captured by Wei.

sentences.zh: 弟定僭號於平涼，遂為魏所滅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ding usurped the title at Pingliang and was thereupon destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ding seized power at Pingliang and was destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 自勃勃至定，凡二十有六載而亡。

translations.literal: From Bobo to Ding, altogether twenty-six years and perished.
translations.idiomatic: From Bobo to Ding was twenty-six years, then extinction.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: Critical Praise
translations.idiomatic: Critical Praise

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：赫連勃勃犬熏醜種類，入居邊宇，屬中壤分崩，緣間肆慝，控弦鳴鏑，據有朔方。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Helian Bobo was a dog-stench ugly species who entered and dwelt in the border territories; when the central plains split apart he seized the interval and unleashed wickedness, controlling the bent bow and sounding the arrow-whistle, holding You and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Helian Bobo was a barbarian breed who seized the north when the central plains split, sounding bow and whistle across Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 遂乃法玄象以開宮，擬神京而建社，竊先王之徽號，備中國之禮容，驅駕英賢，窺窬天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he patterned the dark image to open palaces, modeled the divine capital to build the altars, stole the honored titles of former kings, prepared the ritual and bearing of China, drove and harnessed worthy men, and peered covetously at the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He patterned palaces on the divine capital, stole kings' titles, aped Chinese ritual, and eyed the realm.

sentences.zh: 然其器識高爽，風骨魁奇，姚興睹之而醉心，宋祖聞之而動色。

translations.literal: Yet his capacity and insight were lofty and clear, his wind and bone outstanding and strange; Yao Xing saw him and was intoxicated in heart, Emperor Wu of Song heard and was moved in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his insight was keen and his bearing remarkable; Yao Xing marveled and Liu Yu was stirred.

sentences.zh: 豈陰山之韞異氣，不然何以致斯乎！

translations.literal: Was it that the Yin Mountains stored strange breath—if not, how reach this!
translations.idiomatic: Did the Yin Mountains breed strange spirit—how else produce such a man!

sentences.zh: 雖雄略過人，而凶殘未革，飾非距諫，酷害朝臣，部內囂然，忠良捲舌。

translations.literal: Though his bold strategy surpassed others, his fierce cruelty was not reformed; he adorned wrong and rejected remonstrance, cruelly harmed court ministers; within the departments there was clamor and loyal men curled their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Though his strategy surpassed others, cruelty remained; he rejected remonstrance and harmed ministers until loyalty fell silent.

sentences.zh: 滅亡之禍，宜在厥身，猶及其嗣，非不幸也。

translations.literal: The calamity of extinction should have been on his person—yet it reached his heirs; this was not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Destruction should have fallen on him alone—yet it reached his heirs; that was no accident.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：淳維遠裔，名王之餘。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Chunwei, distant descendant, surplus of a name-king.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Chunwei, distant scion of kings.

sentences.zh: 嘯群龍漠，乘釁侵漁。

translations.literal: Howling with the dragons of the desert, seizing the chance to raid and fish.
translations.idiomatic: He howled with desert dragons and seized the chance to raid.

sentences.zh: 爰創宮宇，易彼氈廬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he created palaces and halls, changing those felt tents.
translations.idiomatic: He built palaces and halls in place of felt tents.

sentences.zh: 雖弄神器，猶曰凶渠。

translations.literal: Though he wielded the divine regalia, he was still called a felonious chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Though he wielded the imperial regalia, he was still called a treacherous bandit chief.
